note: Metrics only. No document text, no page images, no corpus or source file paths. Corpus identified bibliographically.

feature.rust: SidecarPasses::detached_greek_accents; all three passes are on argv and in the job fingerprint
feature.algorithm: Detect a short, low-minimum-confidence, mark-only line whose box sits inside the top of a Greek-dominant base line and overlaps it horizontally. Crop band+base as one region, re-recognize with grc at PSM 13 and native resolution, and replace the base line only if the candidate passes containment, coverage, Greek/Latin/digit retention, confidence and NFC gates. Otherwise keep the base line's combined reading and suppress the mark-only band alone.
feature.detection_is_geometric: Height ratio, minimum word confidence, vertical containment, horizontal overlap and script counts only. The characters a band happens to emit are never the criterion.

ablation_four_real_greek_pages.ground_truth: publisher text layer of a born-digital Teubner-set Greek edition
ablation_four_real_greek_pages.chosen: union crop, grc, PSM 13, native resolution
ablation_four_real_greek_pages.why: PSM 13 measured best; PSM 6 was far worse because it re-runs layout analysis on a crop that is a single line by construction. Upscaling measured slightly worse at 1.5x and 2.0x.

folded_cer.note: ϑ/θ and ϕ/φ folded for evaluation only; OCR output is unchanged

lines.note: the 16 removed lines are exactly the detected mark-only bands

per_page.note: no candidates; byte-identical, which is the control

artifact_suppression_versus_diacritic_re.statement: These are different gains and are not conflated. Suppressing the band removes noise and recovers nothing: measured alone it moves raw CER 0.1756 -> 0.1177 while diacritic errors stay at 81 and script confusions at 137. Re-recognition is what recovers, and only where the safety gates allow it.

recovery_available_if_gates_were_loosene.note: The unconstrained ablation reaches 61, but only by accepting candidates that drop Latin. Most rejections are `latin-lost`, where the base line's Latin is itself corrupted Greek. The strict gate was kept and the smaller recovery reported rather than relaxing a safety condition.

cgpg_full_holdout.finding: Identical. The Patrologia Graeca typeface does not produce detached accent bands, so the pass finds no candidates. Hard gates met — no regression on CER, diacritics, missing or extra lines — but no gain either. The pass is specific to the Teubner-style face it was measured on.
caveats: This holdout has been observed in earlier rounds; it is no longer a pristine blind test.
Every transcribed CGPG region is Greek, so it cannot demonstrate Latin safety.

german_and_latin_regression.finding: The pass is inert on every non-Greek-base page tested.

160_page_book_defaults_all_off.finding: Baseline exactly preserved with all three optional passes off.

limitations: Calibrated and measured on a single real Teubner-set source.
CGPG shows no effect at all, so the gain does not generalise on current evidence.
Most of the measured gain is artifact suppression, not diacritic recovery.
Default off; enabling it is a deliberate opt-in.
